analysis.title: Best of Wire - G10 events guide and gameplan (repost)
key_insights: Five central bank decisions in 72 hours (FOMC, ECB, BoC, BoJ on hold expected, RBNZ hike expected), plus UK Autumn Budget and a CPI print. Megacap earnings and month-end flows are expected to keep trading volatile.

UK Autumn Budget: Citi Research expects a market-friendly budget with fiscal headroom of £14-15bn, down from £23.6bn, via targeted revenue measures including a bank surcharge increase from 3% to 4.5%. Headroom below £10bn would be negative.

DMO remit: Citi strategists expect funding to rise by £11bn, with +£5bn via gilts (to £251.2bn) and +£6bn via Treasury bills. The shift shorter may ease near-term pressure but does little for longer-term yields.

BoC: OIS prices a strong chance of a hike, while Citi economists expect a hold at 2.25%. Bloomberg economists are split 17/35 between hike and hold. A 25bp hike framed as risk management cannot be ruled out.
If the BoC holds, hawkish guidance would keep market pricing near +35bp into year-end and 107bp into Sep 2027. Acknowledging a softer labor market and excess supply would read as most dovish.

FOMC: widely expected to hold with 2bps priced and no SEP update. Citi's house view is one final 25bp hike in Dec and cuts resuming in mid-2027. The key question is whether Warsh acknowledges tighter financial conditions after the AI-led equity selloff.
FOMC equity options imply the largest FOMC-related move since mid-2025 (+/- 90bps), driven largely by megacap earnings after the close. Citi economists expect Thursday GDP to jump toward 3.1%.

ECB: widely expected to hold. Focus is on whether Lagarde addresses French spread weakness and ECB tools, and on signals about a possible early resignation. A Dec hike is Citi's base case. De Cos and Knot are seen as the likeliest successors.

BoJ: expected to hold at 1.25% with Takata dissenting for a hike. Citi expects a 25bp hike in December (OIS prices 20bp) and quarterly hikes toward a 2.0% terminal rate by mid-2027. Implied event move of 52bp makes it the week's biggest risk event.

Australia CPI: Citi expects headline at 0.6% MoM, below consensus, with trimmed mean near 1.0% QoQ (3.6% YoY) from 0.8% prior. OIS prices about 60% odds of an RBA hike next week, which Citi's trader sees closer to 75-80%.

RBNZ: 25bp hike expected and fully priced, with 3.00% seen as the terminal rate. Three more hikes are priced into 2027 (113bp into Sep per Bloomberg WIRP), so risks are dovish. Event jump risk is 52.5bp.

earnings_insights: Megacap earnings after the close on FOMC day are cited as the main driver of the implied equity move of +/- 90bps. No specific EPS or revenue figures are given.

tension_points.bull_case: OIS prices a strong probability of a 20bp hike and Bloomberg economists are split 17/35. The bank has a penchant for surprise and could frame a hike as risk management.
tension_points.bear_case: Citi economists expect a hold at 2.25%, with officials inclined to wait to see how higher rates affect the economy.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A BoC hike would invalidate Citi's hold call.

tension_points.bull_case: A 25bp hike is fully priced and Q4 CPI is expected to be stronger, which makes a pre-emptive hike sensible.
tension_points.bear_case: Three more hikes priced into 2027 leave room for disappointment given high unemployment and slowing GDP.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A statement that signals a terminal rate at 3.00% would deliver the dovish outcome.
